record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in the Theory of Computation as Questions about Two-Way Deterministic Pushdown Automaton Languages
record.original_question: What exact inclusion or equality relationship holds between 2DPDA, the class of two-way deterministic pushdown automaton languages, and DLOG, the class of deterministic logarithmic-space languages?

evidence.quote: 5. What is the relationship between 2DPDA and DLOG?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let 2DPDA denote the class of languages accepted by two-way deterministic pushdown automata. Such a machine has a read-only input tape with endmarkers on which a two-way head moves, together with an unbounded pushdown stack, and operates by a deterministic transition function; a string is accepted when the machine halts in an accepting state. Let DLOG (also written L or DLOGSPACE) denote the class of languages decided by deterministic Turing machines using O(log n) space on a read/write work tape, with a separate read-only input tape of length n.

Determine the exact relationship between these two classes. Specifically, decide which of the following holds and provide a proof:

(a) 2DPDA ⊊ DLOG,
(b) DLOG ⊊ 2DPDA,
(c) 2DPDA = DLOG,
(d) 2DPDA and DLOG are incomparable (each contains a language not in the other).
artifact.status_search_result: The exact relationship between 2DPDA and DLOG remains a long-standing open problem in formal language and complexity theory. It is known that 2DPDA ⊆ P (Cook's theorem) and that DLOG ⊆ P, and connections via auxiliary pushdown automata are well understood, but no proof of inclusion, equality, or incomparability between 2DPDA and DLOG has been established in the literature found.

status_evidence.title: Simulation of Two-Way Pushdown Automata Revisited
status_evidence.snippet: Survey-style discussion of 2DPDA simulation, related to Cook's theorem placing 2DPDA inside P; the precise relation to DLOG is not resolved.
status_evidence.claim: The relation of 2DPDA to logspace classes is discussed but not settled.

status_evidence.title: L (complexity) - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Standard definition of DLOG/L; no known equality or strict inclusion with 2DPDA is reported.
status_evidence.claim: DLOG's relationship to 2DPDA is not listed as resolved.
